questions.question: In the question, a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument. Statement: Should rock shows be allowed to run until midnight at tourist places? Argument I: Yes, more tourists arrive due to rock shows. Tourism is good for the local economy. Argument II: No, local traditions are harmed due to tourism.

questions.solution:
For an argument to be strong, it should directly answer the statement problem.

The argument 'I' is strong because it explains the benefits of allowing rock shows to run till midnight at tourist places as it has a good impact on the economy.

Argument 'II' is not strong because there is no mention of the rock shows instead it argues about tourism.

Hence, only option 1 is correct

questions.question: Present ages of M and N are in the ratio 7 : 8 respectively. After five years this ratio becomes 8 : 9. What is the present age (in years) of M?
questions.questionHtml: Present ages of M and N are in the ratio 7 : 8 respectively. After five years this ratio becomes 8 : 9. What is the present age (in years) of M?
questions.solution:
Let us consider the age of M and N to be 7x : 8x, after 5 years there age will be (7x + 5) and (8x + 5) which is equal to ratio 8 : 9.

(7x + 5) : (8x + 5) ∷ 8 : 9

⇒ 9(7x + 5) = 8 (8x + 5)

⇒ 63x + 45 = 64x + 40

⇒ 45 - 40 = 64x - 63x  ⇒ x = 5

Therefore x = 5, then the age of M will be 7x = 7 × 5 = 35.

questions.question: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tapes are glue. Some glue are paints. All paints are computers. Conclusions: I. Some tapes are paints. II. All glue are paints. III. Some glue are computers.
questions.questionHtml:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some tapes are glue.

Some glue are paints.

All paints are computers.

Conclusions:

I. Some tapes are paints.

II. All glue are paints.

III. Some glue are computers.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

Conclusions:

I. Some tapes are paints → Does not Follow (As, some tapes are glue and some glue are paints. So, it is possible but not definitely true.)

II. All glue are paints → Does not Follow (As, some glue are paints. So, some part of glue is common with paints therefore it is false.)

III. Some glue are computers → Follow (As, some glue are paints and all paints are computers . So, whole paints comes in computers and have some part common with glue therefore it is definitely true.)

So, Only conclusion III follows.

questions.question: Directions: These questions are based on the following information. There are six members in the family; V, W, X, S, T and U but not necessarily in the same way. T is son-in-law of V who is not the mother of S. S and X are children of W. S is the mother of U who not the niece of X who is not the daughter of V. How is X related to T?
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: These questions are based on the following information.

There are six members in the family; V, W, X, S, T and U but not necessarily in the same way. T is son-in-law of V who is not the mother of S. S and X are children of W. S is the mother of U who not the niece of X who is not the daughter of V. How is X related to T?
questions.solution:
From the given information,

Six members of the family; V, W, X, S, T and U.

Explanation with family tree:

References: T is son-in-law of V who is the father of S. S and X are children of W. S is the mother of U who not the niece of X who is not the daughter of V.

Inferences:

1) T is son-in-law of V who is the father of S.

2) S and X are children of W.

3) S is the mother of U who not the niece of X who is not the daughter of V.

Hence, X is the brother-in-law of T.
